newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen higher to limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen higher to limit up.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open up 0.750 to their 2.000-cent limit up, with bellies called up 1.500 to their 3.000-cent limit, according to analysts.

Carryover demand from Monday's mostly limit gains in both contracts following Friday's bullish USDA Hog and Pig should boost prices. The report came as a surprise because it showed producers did not aggressively expand herds in the second quarter as had been expected. This will keep hog and pork supplies well under expectatins for the rest of the year, the analysts said.
The report is most bullish for deferred hogs and pork bellies but nearbys will still show carryover gains with higher cash markets also providing support, they said.

Steady to mostly higher cash hog indications should strengthen nearby hog futures. Hot and humid weather is cutting hog movement and packers are looking for added numbers due to the short kill week, they said.
Cash pork bellies rose to $90 per cwt Monday, the highest level since April 30.
Japan lifted the emergency pork tariff as expected but analysts see no immediate effect.
Pork buying by Japan could be spread over the full third quarter, they said.
